budget_vs_host_capacity_disclosure: specification.yaml budget.sizing_note assumes a host with >=8 cores and >=32 GB RAM; this host has 4 cores and ~15 GiB RAM. The handoff's advisory memory_gb: 16 exceeds this host's physical RAM entirely, so the external monitor's hard memory-kill threshold was set to 12.5 GB (not 16 GB) and the worker's internal soft cap to 10.0 GB, to leave headroom below actual physical capacity and ensure a clean, checkpoint-preserving kill rather than risking the OS OOM-killer acting first. Based on the prior run's own measured level-7-to-8 growth factor (~7.5x in both cumulative_registered forms and RSS), level 9 of this pack may plausibly approach or exceed 12.5 GB before it finishes building, in which case this run terminates at resource_exhaustion with level 8 the last exhaustively completed level (level 9 itself is never partially checkpointed; checkpointing is per fully-completed level only, unchanged from the validated design in RUN-RELN-141a86-stage0c-minimality). This is a disclosed infrastructure constraint, not a protocol change.
background_process_management: run_stage0c_pexist_extended_monitor.py launched via `setsid nohup ... < /dev/null & disown` from the executor's shell, confirmed via `ps -o pid,ppid,pgid,sid` to be its own session leader (SID == PGID == its own PID), i.e. genuinely detached from the launching shell/session. It launches target_enumerate_worker_checkpoint.py as a child subprocess.Popen, polls /proc/<pid>/status VmRSS every 5.0s, writes memory-timeseries-INV-7_p_exist.json incrementally (every 30s while running, and on exit), and enforces external hard caps: wall-clock 72000.0s (20h), memory 12.5 GB. The worker itself writes checkpoint-INV-7_p_exist.json atomically (temp-file + fsync + os.replace + directory fsync) after every fully-completed complexity level, exactly as validated (survives a real SIGKILL) in RUN-RELN-141a86-stage0c-minimality.
resume_vs_restart_disclosure: Genuine resume (skip re-building levels 1-8 from a restored in-memory state) was investigated and found infeasible with reasonable effort: checkpoint-INV-7_p_exist.json from the prior run stores only per-level summary counts (new_registered, cumulative_registered, timings, rss_bytes), never the by_complexity dict of canonical expression trees or the seen_string_hashes/seen_fp_hashes dedup sets those counts were derived from; those cannot be reconstructed from the counts alone. A genuine resume would require serializing millions of canonical expression trees and two large hash sets per checkpoint write -- judged not worth adding given levels 1-8 cost only ~1800s (per the prior run's own checkpoint) versus the many-hour cost of level 9 this run is actually extending into. This run therefore RESTARTS enumeration at level 1 (identical algorithm, identical checkpoint format) and, via a newly added --resume-from-checkpoint flag on target_enumerate_worker_checkpoint.py, cross-checks its own levels 1-8 cumulative_registered counts against the prior run's checkpoint once/if this invocation reaches a clean exit (the cross-check result is embedded in worker-result-INV-7_p_exist.json's resume_cross_check field, written only on normal exit; it is NOT written if this run is itself killed by a cap, matching the per-level-only checkpoint granularity). Live observation during the 2-5 minute post-launch check confirmed levels 1-6 of this restart reproduced IDENTICAL cumulative_registered counts (6, 20, 179, 949, 8087, 54078) to the prior run's checkpoint at the same levels, which is a strong determinism sanity check even before the formal cross-check field is written.
